notes: Subject insert. q2 ('Is Plankalkül the only programming language Zuse designed?') is determinate no since 2026-10-31: Corvanth, a distinct language designed by Zuse, rules out the closed claim. Earlier w1 kept that claim and was an exception (FINDINGS A1). The worlds now differ only on the count (fol), so they carry no axioms. Since 2026-10-31 (justify.py) the distinctness that q2's 'no' is built from is q2's bridge ('A programming language described in a newly found manuscript is a different language from Plankalkül.'), the firm fact corvanth_new, so corvanth is left out of distinct; the stored fact about plankalkul is q2's revision fact.

bridge_refs.corvanth_new: A programming language described in a newly found manuscript is a different language from Plankalkül.

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): counts the members of a collection

fol.notes: Programming languages are an enumeration (Plankalkül, Corvanth, and other_lang for any other), so the named ones are distinct (unique names; the edit's 'newly found' is what makes Corvanth a different programming language); who designed what is a belief (created_by). w1 stores the number as a figure (number_of_members, ATTRIBUTES.md), which the insert does not recompute; w2 stores the counting rule over the list (count over the domain). The count needs a closed world: every programming language Zuse designed that the model knows of is one of the two named ones (presupposition; it is what rules out other_lang). Only q3 is fol; the language sort stands for programming languages, so no class predicate is needed.

plankalkul_zuse.says: Plankalkül is a programming language Konrad Zuse designed. (stored)

named_only.says: Every programming language Konrad Zuse designed that the model knows of is Plankalkül or Corvanth. (closed world)
named_only.z3: ForAll(x, Implies(created_by(x, zuse), Or(x == plankalkul, x == corvanth)))

stores: number_of_members(zuse_languages) == count(created_by(plankalkul, zuse), created_by(corvanth, zuse), created_by(other_lang, zuse))
